answer: An agent economy can make every new identity post a refundable stake before it may vote or receive work, while a random committee of established agents checks whether its behavior matches a claimed role. If one identity breaks the rules, the committee slashes its stake and lowers the sponsor’s reputation; sponsors therefore have reason to audit newcomers. A mirror account, falcon reviewer, or spiral of aliases still requires fresh capital, so multiplying fake identities scales the attacker’s losses linearly.
